Mouvements et Enjeux Sociaux - Revue Internationale des Dynamiques Sociales (Kinshasa: Chaire de Dynamique Sociale, Presses de l'Université de Kinshasa) 126 (janvier-février 2023): 237-243. tone_statements.quote: Pour répondre à un appel, un locuteur topoké utilise le phonème vocalique /e/avec un ton montant (v) : ě qui signifie en français ‘‘oui’’. Pour donner une réponse positive à une interrogation totale on utilise dans la langue en étude le phonème vocalique /e/allongé avec un ton bas (‘‘) : e qui signifie en français ‘‘oui’’. [...] Dans le cas d’une réponse négative, un locuteur topoké lance le phonème /e/ deux fois avec un ton haut ( ’ ) : é, é qui signifie en Français « Non ».
tone_statements.translation: To answer a call, a Topoké speaker uses the vowel phoneme /e/ with a rising tone: ě, meaning 'yes'. To give a positive answer to a yes/no question one uses the lengthened vowel /e/ with a low tone: e, meaning 'yes'. [...] For a negative answer, a Topoké speaker utters the phoneme /e/ twice with a high tone: é, é, meaning 'No'.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: H, L and a rising tone on /e/ mentioned; no inventory given

tone_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2012. Contributions aux études linguistiques sur le haut Congo: esquisses du soa, mbesa, tofoké et lokelé. (ILCAA Language Monograph Series, 6.) Fuchu/Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. xvii+266 pp. Ch. 4 'Le parler tofoké de Yangole', pp. 139-192.
tone_statements.quote: 4.2.3. Tons en tofoké de Yangole Il existe deux tons de base: ton bas et ton haut. Les exemples abondent dans les sections précédentes. Les régles qui expliquent comment de ces tons simples on peut obtenir des tons complexes sont exposées dans la morphonologie. Les tons complexes sont encore observables dans quelques petits mots. [...] Exemple d'oppostion tonale: [...] bolili 'fumée' vs. bolili 'allié' [...] 4.3.3. Morphotonémes. Les principales régles de représentation de tons sont les suivantes: fusion, absorption, harmonie, métatonie, dissimilation, polarité et projection. Fusion tonale [...] °H-H > H, °B-B > B, °H-B > D, °B-H > M.
tone_statements.translation: 4.2.3. Tones in Yangole Tofoké. There are two basic tones: low tone and high tone. Examples abound in the preceding sections. The rules explaining how complex tones can be obtained from these simple tones are set out in the morphonology. Complex tones are still observable in a few small words. [...] Example of tonal opposition: bolili 'smoke' vs. bolili 'ally' [tone marks lost in scanned] [...] 4.3.3. Morphotonemes. The main tone-representation rules are: fusion, absorption, harmony, metatony, dissimilation, polarity and projection. Tonal fusion: H-H > H, L-L > L, H-L > Falling, L-H > Rising.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H, B=L); falling and rising as fused complexes

tone_statements.citation: Stoop, Henk. 1989b. Les préfixes du sogo (C53). Annales Aequatoria 10: 127-140.
tone_statements.quote: 1.3. A la contraction de tons différents, le haut, noté ´ l'emporte généralement sur le bas, non marqué. Le ton instable, marqué ' , se comporte généralement comme le bas, mais en d'autres cas il a une réalisation particulière. Le ton qui est noté H ou B au côté gauche d'un morphème s'appelle ton flottant; il remplace le ton du morphème avec lequel il entre en contact, dans notre cas celui du préfixe.
tone_statements.translation: 1.3. When different tones contract, the high tone (marked with an acute) generally prevails over the low, which is unmarked. The unstable tone (marked ') generally behaves like the low, but in other cases it has a particular realisation. The tone written H or B [L] on the left side of a morpheme is called a floating tone; it replaces the tone of the morpheme it comes into contact with, in our case that of the prefix.
tone_statements.locator: p. 130, §1.3 (section 1 'Un peu de phonologie' begins p. 129)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H vs unmarked L) plus an 'unstable' tone and floating H/L

tone_statements.citation: Harries, Lyndon. 1955. Grammar of Gesogo. Kongo-Overzee 21: 420-440.
tone_statements.quote: Tonal Data. 4.1. Gesogo is a language with lexical tone. The alternance of tone on verbal radicals is hidden in the infinitive, but is regularly observed in both affırmative and negative tenses. 1.2. [=4.2] Nominals can be elassified into four tone-groups according to the tone of the radical and suflix. 4.3. The tone-pattern of words is maintained in all observed syntactical positions 4.4. An acute accent (’) marks a high tone, and an unmarked syllable denotes a normal low tone. A circumflex accent (*) indicates a falling tone, and an inverted eircumflex accent denotes a rising tone. A mid-tone is a slipped high tone and is marked with a grave accent (‘).
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 basic (H, L) plus falling, rising on long vowels and a mid = 'slipped high'

sources.note: Syntax of minor and passive sentences in topoké with tone-marked examples (acute = H, unmarked = L); the only tonal remarks are that the response particles are distinguished by tone alone -- /e/ with rising tone 'yes (to a call)', lengthened /e/ with low tone 'yes (polar question)', é é with high tone 'no' (p. 238 sec. 1.1); no inventory, no rules, no statement on the tone system; the rising tone is on a monosyllabic interjection and is not evidence about contour tones in the lexicon.
